package_info.package_versions: All known versions (Win32/Spacecolon.A, Win64/Spacecolon.A, Win64/DelShad.D, Win32/Filecoder.FS, Win32/Filecoder.Spacecolon.A)
package_info.why_malicious: Spacecolon is a modular toolset used by the CosmicBeetle threat actor to gain unauthorized access, maintain persistence, deploy ransomware (Scarab, ScRansom), and exfiltrate data. It provides remote access, executes arbitrary commands, disables security products, and delivers ransomware, all without user consent. Its components (ScHackTool, ScInstaller, ScService) are designed for post-exploitation, lateral movement, and destructive payload delivery.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ScHackTool loads and executes third-party tools to disable security products, extract credentials, and escalate privileges. It can deploy additional payloads (ScInstaller, ScService) and execute arbitrary commands received from the operator.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial compromise, the code executes as a service or process, loads and runs red team tools (e.g., credential dumpers, AV killers), and deploys further payloads, enabling lateral movement and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The orchestrator's ability to load arbitrary tools, disable security, and deploy further malware is highly indicative of post-exploitation frameworks used by threat actors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate administrative tools do not covertly deploy malware or disable security controls without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Red team frameworks in controlled penetration tests may use similar orchestration, but with explicit authorization.
key_indicators: Execution of multiple third-party hacking tools

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ScInstaller installs ScService as a persistent Windows service, configuring it to start automatically and run with elevated privileges.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the code writes the ScService binary to disk, registers it as a Windows service, and sets it to auto-start, ensuring persistence for remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installing unauthorized services for persistence is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not install backdoor services without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software may install services, but with user approval and clear documentation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ScService acts as a backdoor, connecting to C&C servers, executing commands, downloading and running payloads, and collecting system information.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service start and during runtime, the code establishes outbound connections to hardcoded C&C domains, receives and executes arbitrary commands, downloads additional malware, and exfiltrates system data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Backdoor functionality with C&C communication, arbitrary command execution, and data exfiltration is a hallmark of remote access trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate services do not connect to unknown C&C servers or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may have similar features, but only in trusted, managed environments.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to known malicious C&C infrastructure
Ability to download and execute further payloads

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Ransomware payload encrypts user files, appends custom extensions, and drops ransom notes demanding payment for decryption.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed, the code enumerates files on local and network drives, encrypts them using strong cryptography, renames files with a new extension, and creates ransom notes in affected directories.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: File encryption and ransom note creation are definitive ransomware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should encrypt user files and demand payment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup software may encrypt files, but never for extortion.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Deletes Windows Shadow Copies to prevent file recovery after ransomware encryption.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Before or during ransomware execution, the code issues system commands to delete all Volume Shadow Copies, removing backup restore points.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting shadow copies is a common anti-recovery tactic in ransomware attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not delete all system backups without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup management tools may delete old shadow copies, but with user approval.
key_indicators: Systematic deletion of all shadow copies

attack_chain.action: Initial compromise of target system via ZeroLogon exploit or RDP brute force.
Deployment and execution of ScHackTool to orchestrate further actions and deploy additional tools.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disabling security, credential extraction, and deployment of ScInstaller

attack_chain.action: Installation of ScService for persistent remote access.
ScService connects to C&C, executes commands, downloads payloads, and exfiltrates data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware deployment or further lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Deployment of ransomware payload (Scarab/ScRansom) to encrypt files and demand ransom.
Deletion of Windows Shadow Copies to prevent recovery.
attack_chain.leads_to: Irreversible data loss unless ransom is paid

behavioral_signatures: Execution of unknown PE files named app.exe, ap.exe, Taskmgr.exe, a.exe, installer.exe, svcss.exe, svvc.exe, 1new.exe, kkk.exe, Project1.exe, Shadow.exe
Installation of unauthorized Windows services with auto-start
Outbound connections to known Spacecolon C&C domains/IPs
Mass file encryption and ransom note creation
Systematic deletion of Volume Shadow Copies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of suspicious PE files matching known Spacecolon component names and hashes. Detect unauthorized installation of Windows services, especially those set to auto-start and running from non-standard locations. Alert on outbound connections to known Spacecolon C&C domains and IPs. Look for mass file encryption activity, creation of ransom notes, and deletion of shadow copies. Correlate these behaviors to identify the full attack chain and block further malicious activity.
